findings.evidence: Lines 225-228: `(hz : z ∈ euclideanSection d) (hnull : complexMinkowskiProduct z z = 0) : z = 0`. Naming conventions: hypotheses needed to convey the intended reference are listed after `of`, in the order they appear (`add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le`, `lt_of_le_of_ne`).
findings.fix: Include the null hypothesis, e.g. `eq_zero_of_mem_euclideanSection_of_complexMinkowskiProduct_self_eq_zero` (and the `closure` variant), or restate as an iff characterising nullness on the section.
findings.issue: `eq_zero_of_mem_euclideanSection` names only `hz : z ∈ euclideanSection d` and omits `hnull : complexMinkowskiProduct z z = 0`, so the name reads as "every point of the Euclidean section is zero", which is false. Same at line 231 for `eq_zero_of_mem_closure_euclideanSection`.

findings.evidence: Lines 251-253 vs. `mem_euclideanSection_iff : z ∈ euclideanSection d ↔ (z (Sum.inl 0)).re = 0 ∧ ∀ i, (z (Sum.inr i)).im = 0`, satisfied by `ofMinkowski v` whenever `v (Sum.inl 0) = 0`.
findings.fix: Rename to `ofMinkowski_notMem_euclideanSection_of_causalCharacter_eq_lightLike` (plus the nonzero condition), keeping both hypotheses visible.
findings.issue: `ofMinkowski_not_mem_euclideanSection` names neither `hv : causalCharacter v = .lightLike` nor `hne : v ≠ 0`; as named it claims no real Minkowski vector ever lies on the Euclidean section, which is false (any `v` with zero time component is in the image, by `mem_euclideanSection_iff` at line 174).

findings.evidence: Naming-conventions dictionary: `∉` → `notMem`. `grep -c 'theorem .*_notMem_\|theorem notMem_' mathlib/Mathlib` → 281 occurrences across 177 files; the `not_mem_` spelling survives in only 4 files (e.g. `Mathlib/ModelTheory/Types.lean`).
findings.issue: `not_mem` is the retired spelling for `∉`; current Mathlib uses `notMem`.

findings.evidence: Lines 238-240: hypotheses `(hv : ofMinkowski v ∈ euclideanSection d) (hne : v ≠ 0)`; only the first appears in the name.
findings.issue: `causalCharacter_eq_spaceLike_of_ofMinkowski_mem_euclideanSection` omits `hne : v ≠ 0`; without it the named claim is false, since `v = 0` lies on the section and is not spacelike.

summary: Three theorem names drop the hypothesis that carries the mathematics, so each name asserts a blanket statement that is false (every section element is zero; no Minkowski vector lies on the Euclidean section). One name also uses the retired `not_mem` spelling.
